questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

I goes to / attend dance classes at / the National Dance Academy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the verb 'goes' is incorrect.
 
• The subject **'I'** is **first person singular** and should be used with the verb **'go'** to form **'I go'**.
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be 'go' instead of 'goes'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *I go to attend dance classes at the National Dance Academy*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The subject **'I'** always takes the base form of the verb without the 's' ending.
 
• In English, the third person singular pronouns (he, she, it) are the ones that take a verb with an 's' ending in the present simple tense.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I noticed that they / did not went to / the museum but entered / a shopping complex.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the phrase 'did not went' is incorrect.
 
• The correct form should be 'did not go' because when using 'did' in the past tense, the base form of the verb 'go' should be used, not the past form 'went'.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be 'did not go'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *I noticed that they did not go to the museum but entered a shopping complex.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Whenever 'did' is used in a question or negative sentence in the past tense, the main verb should be in its base form.
 
• Example: She did not eat the cake. (Not: She did not ate the cake.)
 
• Similarly: Did they go to the museum? (Not: Did they went to the museum?)

questions.question:
Select the option that corrects the following sentence.

He has broken his leg yesterday.

options.text: He has broke his leg yesterday.
He have broken his leg yesterday.
He had broke his leg yesterday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e., He broke his leg yesterday.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence "He has broken his leg yesterday" is incorrect due to the use of the present perfect tense with a specific past time reference (**'yesterday'**).
 
• The correct way to refer to a specific time in the past (**'yesterday'**) is by using the **simple past tense**.
 
• Therefore, we should say "He broke his leg yesterday.".

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *He broke his leg yesterday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The present perfect tense (has/have + past participle) is used to describe actions that have occurred at an unspecified time before now, not specific past times like 'yesterday'.
 
 
• **Example**: He has broken his leg. (unspecified time)
 
 
 
• Simple past is used for actions completed at a specific time in the past.
 
 
• **Example**: He broke his leg last week. (specific time)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Rimjhim received __a children’s very illustrated colourful atlas__ on her 10th birthday.

options.text: a very illustrated colourful atlas children
a colourful very illustrated children’s atla
a very colourful illustrated children’s atlas
an very illustrated colourful children’s atlas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e., a very colourful illustrated children’s atlas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence "Rimjhim received a children’s very illustrated colourful atlas on her 10th birthday" is incorrect due to the improper order of adjectives.
 
• The order of adjectives in English typically follows this sequence: quantity, quality, size, age, shape, color, proper adjective (often nationality, other place of origin, or material), and purpose or qualifier.
 
• Accordingly, "very" (emphasizer) should come first, then "colourful" (quality), and finally "illustrated" (participle acting as an adjective).
 
• Therefore, the phrase should be "a very colourful illustrated children’s atlas."

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *Rimjhim received a very colourful illustrated children’s atlas on her 10th birthday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The rules for the correct order of adjectives ensure clear and natural-sounding descriptions in English.
 
 
• **Example**: She bought a beautiful large old round wooden table.
 
 
 
• This sequence helps in maintaining a logical and readable structure in sentences that include multiple adjectives.

questions.question: The average monthly expenditure of a family was Rs. 2,500 during the first 4 months, Rs. 2,750 during the next 5 months and Rs. 3,550 during the last 3 months of a year. If the total saving during the year was Rs. 5,500, what was the average monthly income of the family?

questions.question: How do the muscle cells help in movement?

options.text: The blood flow of the cells helps in movement.

The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement.

questions.solution:

• This is the correct mechanism as muscle cells, also known as muscle fibers, contract and relax to produce movement.
 
• Muscle contraction is initiated by signals from the nervous system and involves the interaction of actin and myosin filaments within the muscle cells.
 
• This process requires energy in the form of ATP, which is produced by cellular respiration.
 
• Relaxation occurs when the muscle cells stop receiving signals from the nervous system, allowing the muscle fibers to lengthen and return to their resting state.

• There are three types of muscle tissue: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth. Each type has a specific function and structure.
 
• Skeletal muscles are responsible for voluntary movements, cardiac muscles are found in the heart and are responsible for pumping blood, and smooth muscles are found in various internal organs and help in involuntary movements such as digestion.
 
• Proper muscle function is essential for overall mobility, stability, and the performance of various bodily functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 20** of the Constitution of India provides protection in respect of conviction for offenses.
 
• This article ensures certain protections against arbitrary and unjust prosecution and punishment.
 
• It includes **protection against ex post facto laws**, which means an individual cannot be convicted of an act that was not a crime at the time it was committed.
 
• It also protects against double jeopardy, meaning a person cannot be prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once.
 
• Additionally, it provides protection against self-incrimination, ensuring that no person accused of any offense shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
